differences.what: massing: a light stone front over a raised basement, the principal storey and the foot of the second, the canted bay and the recessed north part with the porch, seen square-on
differences.how: T-3166: the 1911 sheet's 19.4 x 8.2 m front block on K01 with K02's smooth Lemont ashlar front, the principal floor 2.3 m and the storeys 5.6 and 4.4 m, read through this camera

differences.what: the canted bay through the basement and both storeys, one tall window in its south cheek (x 190-250 px) and one in its front (x 300-365), each under a small moulded cap
differences.how: T-3166: a K08 canted bay 4.54 m at the wall and 1.25 m out, its front 1.92 m, one window a storey in each cheek and in the front, 1.05 x 3.5 m on the principal storey, under K09's cornice-hood lintels; they render within about 10 px

differences.what: the basement windows under the principal ones, about y 505-580 px (about 0.3-1.45 m over grade): T-1887 cuts one under each of the bay's three principal lights, as wide as they are, iron uprights in their reveals, the bay's plinth lowered to 0.15 m so that it runs under them; they render in place and size through the fence
the porch: columns at the stoop's head, a deep carved entablature (y 140-215 px) under a cornice, a balustrade on its top (y 100-140), its floor at the principal floor
differences.how: T-3166: K01's door hood on two columns (T-2963), 2.4 m wide and 1.8 m out, its soffit 6.0 m and its fascia 1.0 m; the entablature and the balustrade render within about 10 px

differences.what: the porch's round arches on its front and its south side, springing from the capitals at y 245 px (about 5.45 m) to crowns at y 212 (about 5.95 m) under the carved spandrel: T-1887 turns them (K01's porch arcade), and they render in place on both faces

the third column at the porch's south-rear corner (x 440 px), a round column with a capital against the canted bay's north cheek, and the porch's south end carried back on a diagonal from its front corner over the south column (x 512) to the cheek (the entablature's end at x 418): T-1887 builds K01's splayed porch end, the hood's fascia, slab and balustrade returning on the diagonal to the cheek 1.06 m south of the hood's end and 0.95 m out, on a third column 0.92 m out at v 4.28, which renders at x 445; the south arch is turned on the diagonal from it to the south column

the terrace south of the stoop under the porch's south arch, its front a solid stone parapet pierced by a row of four upright slots (x 440-500, y 433-473): T-1887 lays it at the landing's height to v 4.0, its parapet 0.8 m high with four 0.1 x 0.2 m slots, which renders at x 444-500
the porch's carving: the entablature's carved frieze, the spandrels over the arches, the columns' capitals
differences.how: T-3168: built plain: K01's hood fascia and square capital blocks under the entablature; carving is relief of a few centimetres on the right members, the entablature's and the capitals' places and sizes within about 10 px, under the T-3153 bar

differences.what: the porch's balustrade in stone with turned balusters, heavier than the build's
differences.how: T-3168: the porch laid columns, entablature and balustrade in the front's stone (T-3159's portico fabric), its balustrade 0.65 m high on 0.3 m posts with 0.1 m balusters under a 0.25 m rail; the balusters are square where the print's are turned, under a foot (the partial view reads the same balustrade as solid panels: the two prints disagree on its fill)

differences.what: the stoop's cheeks: solid stone parapets carried down beside the flight with turned balusters on their tops, and a newel at the foot
differences.how: T-3168: a turned stone balustrade on both cheeks' tops, 0.9 m over the nosings, with newels at the landing and at the foot (entrance_kit.balustrade); the partial view reads the cheeks as solid parapets with blocks at the foot, so the two prints disagree on the fill over the cheek

differences.what: the panelled stone pilasters framing the bay's faces (x 145-160, 285-300, 385-400 px), and the carved panels between the storeys
differences.how: built as plain ashlar on the bay's angles and between its storeys at the print's places; the panels and the carved panels are surface relief of a few centimetres, under the T-3153 bar

differences.what: the walls round the corner from the front: light stone, as the front, at the print's left edge
differences.how: T-1887: the build laid 1828's flanks in buff brick; the 1911 sheet draws the three-storey block's north, east and south walls in one blue (stone) band, the range behind it pink (brick), so both flanks are laid in the front's Lemont ashlar 14.0 m back (stone_front.flanks.to_m) and the stone-drawn canted bay on the south flank in the same stone

differences.what: no opening in the print's left band (x 0-150 px): the build's two south-flank windows in front of the canted flank bay (2.8 and 5.8 m from the corner) rendered there
differences.how: T-1887: side_bays emptied, so the flank's first 8 m stand blank in the front's stone; through T-3166's camera the 5.8 m window had rendered at x 100-116, and with the principal point 300 px further left both did (x 60-80 and 105-125)

differences.what: the light stone face south of the bay's cheek at the print's left edge (x 0-150 px) with a pilaster at x 40-60: the print shows front wall south of the bay, where the 1911 sheet's trace starts the bay's cheek at the house's south corner
differences.how: T-1887 (2026-11-14): built as a plain stone range on the south flank at the front, 2.25 m out and 4.0 m along the flank, full height under the front's cornice, with no window in its street face (house_1828_prairie bays.south_front_range; L-k01-1828-shipman-1887). The 1911 sheet does not draw it, but three sources do: this print; the Rand McNally view of 1893 (rand_mcnally_1893_views_prairie_west_1816_1936), which draws a plain windowless strip at the south end of 1828's front beside the bay's windows, with the shaded south flank behind it; and D. B. Shipman's permit (Chicago Tribune, 9 July 1876, on Chicagology's page), which gives the house a 35 ft (10.67 m) front against the sheet's 8.2 m, 2.47 m more where this print reads 2.25. That also settles the earlier 'convex' reading. The lit strip at x 47-87 is the range's street face at its south corner, catching the sun past the street trees whose shadow covers x 90-145. Its courses across x 8-48 rise to the right and vanish with 1824's south-flank frieze (x -1200 to -2500 against -1380 and -1473), which is what a face running back along the flanks does: the range's south face. Re-rendered: a light, windowless stone face from x 37 to the bay's cheek at x 175, full height, where the print shows one from its corner at about x 44 to the cheek at 145.

differences.what: the second storey and the mansard: the frame cuts them off
differences.how: read off the partial view (glessner_partial.json, solved by T-3168), whose match record carries them

differences.what: the iron fence on a stone curb before the house, with tall turned posts at its gate
differences.how: K11's spear fence on its curb 7.4 m before the front, its posts square; the print's posts are turned, under a foot of difference in size

differences.what: the front's colour
differences.how: the print is monochrome; it reads light, and K02's Lemont limestone renders a warm buff: the tone is the Inter Ocean's 'light stone-front'

differences.what: the flanks, the round bay and the canted bay on the south flank, and the rear range
differences.how: the camera is square to the front; built to the 1911 sheet at the reconstructed tier (L-k01-1828-shipman-1887)

differences.what: the walk and the entrance gate
differences.how: T-3206 adds the K14 walk and stands the entrance gate open, with a cinder walk down the side passage

differences.what: the boundary's kind
differences.how: this print shows an iron fence on a curb; glessner_partial reads as a low solid wall; the fence is kept (L-k14-walks-1800-block-3206)

differences.what: the range's street face is channelled in the print (horizontal joints a few centimetres deep, about 0.6 m apart, read across x 90-140 in shade) and smooth in the render
differences.how: T-1887 (2026-11-14): the range is laid in the front's smooth Lemont ashlar. K01 dresses a stone front and its flanks only smooth or rock-faced (stone_front.dressing), and a K08 bay's face takes no channelled dressing, so the print's channelling is not built yet. It is the same light stone and the same plain face, but a visitor at the curb would see the joints, so the item stays open.

differences.what: the range's south face and corner: the print shows light stone receding from about x 44 to the frame's edge (x 8); the render turns the corner at x 37 and shows its south face only as a sliver, with sky beyond
differences.how: the principal point's open question (T-3166's square camera puts it at the print's edge, which makes a face running along the flanks vanish at x 0; the courses here and 1824's frieze vanish near x -1450). Two camera fits disagree about it (T-3153). The corner itself, x 37 against about 44, is 7 px, about 0.1 m.

differences.what: the cheek's junction with the range: print x 145, render x 175
differences.how: 30 px, about 0.5 m at the bay; it is the trade between the bay cheek's width and the eye's v that T-3166's solve records (10-15 px per 4 m of eye), and the 1911 sheet's 0.3 m corner pier the K01 bay keeps. Two camera fits disagree about it, so it does not move the plan.

differences.what: the front's belt course between the storeys carried across the range's street face (render y about 135), which the print does not show on the band
differences.how: a course a few centimetres proud, under 0.3 m, in the trees' shade in the print.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
